evidence.note: April 5, 1956 Medford Mail Tribune, printed/PDF page 3, United Press report reproduces FBI announcement identifying John Cyril Hellman, Butte Communist organizer for Montana/Idaho, born December 26, 1921 at Columbia Falls. Original page visually checked.

FBI deceased-records index, PDF page 296, explicitly gives JOHN CYRIL HELLMAN birth 12/26/1921 and death 8/7/2007. Original index page visually checked; full name and birth match the contemporary arrest report. No dates taken from generic John Hellman namesakes.

Lawson, Your Trial, Masses & Mainstream July 1948, printed page 3/PDF page 5, explicitly states his May 21, 1948 sentencing. Author contemporary first-person account; original page visually checked. This is the sentence for the case whose actual custody occurred in 1950-1951; existing incarceration/release dates unchanged.

Daily Iowan May 22, 1948, page 4, Associated Press report corroborates Lawson and Trumbo sentenced yesterday, with appeal bond. Verdict and sentencing distinguished; no arrest or actual service date inferred.

John H. Calhoun outside Big Bethel AME Church, Atlanta, April 20, 1983. Nick Arroyo, Atlanta Journal-Constitution Photographic Archives, Georgia State University Library, AJCP363-030b. Archive metadata identifies the subject; AUC NAACP papers corroborate identity. Archive permits educational use without permission. Full original JPEG retained, including copyright notice; no claim of public-domain status. Conflicting birth-year authority metadata is not used to change existing vitals.

National Guardian April 25, 1955, printed/PDF page 4, photograph of the four Doty brothers reporting to jail. Original source caption and matching publisher caption reviewed for individual identification; see the shared ordering note in CREDITS-batch442.md. Photographer Larry Schreiber, Minneapolis newspaper photograph. Native grayscale /Im0 JPX 4192x5576; exact rectangular crop isolates the identified brother. No age-derived birthdate added.

National Guardian April 25, 1955, printed/PDF page 4, contemporary photo caption individually names the four Doty brothers and expressly says they went to jail March 29, 1955. This is actual commencement of the second, refusing-induction prison term. Earlier refusal-to-register imprisonment is separate. No arrest date, sentencing date or calculated two-year release added.
